archivedDraft.scene: A traveler with a laptop checks a café’s work and seating policy.

sourceCards.sourceNoteInternal: Many people in Mexico and the US also just say "laptop".
Usually pronounced "wai-fai" in Mexico and the US.
An inside corner of a room, the kind of place you'd sit.
In Mexico this covers sweet breads like conchas.

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: ¿Le molesta si me quedo a trabajar 2 horas?
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: Do you mind if I stay and work for 2 hours?
sourceCards.sourceNoteInternal: Using usted (le) keeps it polite with staff.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: ここで2時間作業してもよろしいですか？
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Do you mind if I stay and work for 2 hours?

sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: Wi-Fiのパスワードは何でしょうか？

sourceCards.sourceEnglish: Can I sit near an outlet?
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: コンセントの近くの席に座ってもよろしいですか？
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Can I sit near an outlet?

sourceCards.sourceEnglish: When would you prefer that I order again?
sourceCards.sourceNoteInternal: After "prefiere que" the verb takes the subjunctive: vuelva.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: 次はいつ頃注文したらよろしいでしょうか？
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: When would you prefer that I order again?

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: Si se llena, le dejo la mesa.
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: If it fills up, I'll give up the table.
sourceCards.sourceNoteInternal: Spanish uses the present tense here where English uses "I'll".
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: 満席になったら、テーブルを空けます。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: If it fills up, I'll give up the table.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Es martes por la mañana y Lena entra a un café pequeño con su computadora portátil.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: It is Tuesday morning and Lena walks into a small café with her laptop.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 火曜日の朝、レナはノートパソコンを持って小さなカフェに入ります。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: It is Tuesday morning and Lena walks into a small café with her laptop.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Antes de sentarse, va al mostrador y le pregunta a la mesera: ¿Le molesta si me quedo a trabajar 2 horas?
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Before sitting down, she goes to the counter and asks the server: Do you mind if I stay and work for 2 hours?
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 席に着く前に、レナはカウンターへ行き、女性の店員さんに尋ねます。「ここで2時間作業してもよろしいですか？」
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Before sitting down, she goes to the counter and asks the server: Do you mind if I stay and work for 2 hours?

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: La mesera sonríe y dice: No hay problema, pero a la hora del almuerzo se llena mucho.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: The server smiles and says: No problem, but at lunchtime it gets very full.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 店員さんは笑顔で「大丈夫ですよ。ただ、お昼どきはとても混みます」と言います。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: The server smiles and says: No problem, but at lunchtime it gets very full.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Lena contesta: Si se llena, le dejo la mesa, y luego pregunta: ¿Cuál es la contraseña del wifi?
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Lena answers: If it fills up, I'll give up the table, and then she asks: What is the Wi-Fi password?
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: レナは「満席になったら、テーブルを空けます」と答えてから、「Wi-Fiのパスワードは何でしょうか？」と尋ねます。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Lena answers: If it fills up, I'll give up the table, and then she asks: What is the Wi-Fi password?

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: La mesera le da un papelito con la contraseña y le señala una mesa en el rincón con un enchufe.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: The server gives her a slip of paper with the password and points her to a table in the corner with an outlet.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 店員さんは、パスワードを書いた小さな紙をレナに渡し、コンセントのある隅のテーブルを指し示します。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: The server gives her a slip of paper with the password and points her to a table in the corner with an outlet.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Lena conecta su cargador, pide un café con leche y un pan dulce, y empieza a trabajar.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Lena plugs in her charger, orders a latte and a sweet pastry, and starts working.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: レナは充電器をコンセントに差し込み、カフェラテと甘いパンを注文して、作業を始めます。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Lena plugs in her charger, orders a latte and a sweet pastry, and starts working.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Después de 1 hora, levanta la mano y pregunta: ¿Cuándo prefiere que vuelva a pedir?
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: After 1 hour, she raises her hand and asks: When would you prefer that I order again?
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 1時間後、レナは手を挙げて、「次はいつ頃注文したらよろしいでしょうか？」と尋ねます。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: After 1 hour, she raises her hand and asks: When would you prefer that I order again?

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: La mesera dice: Cuando usted quiera, porque yo paso por su mesa cada media hora.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: The server says: Whenever you like, because I come by your table every half hour.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 店員さんは「お好きなときにどうぞ。30分ごとにお席に伺いますので」と言います。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: The server says: Whenever you like, because I come by your table every half hour.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Al final, Lena pide la cuenta y deja una buena propina por el tiempo y el espacio.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: At the end, Lena asks for the bill and leaves a good tip for the time and the space.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 最後に、レナはお会計をお願いし、時間と場所の分として、多めのチップを置いていきます。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: At the end, Lena asks for the bill and leaves a good tip for the time and the space.

japaneseSpecificFocusCandidate: Ask whether working for two hours is welcome, find the Wi-Fi password and an outlet table, check when to order again, and leave the table if the café fills.
speakingGoalInternal: You need to work for two hours; ask whether that's acceptable, where to sit, and when to order a second round.
speakingGoalJapaneseDraft: カフェで2時間仕事をしたいことを店員に伝え、席とコンセント、Wi-Fiのパスワード、次の注文のタイミングを尋ねてください。
sourceConflictInternal: The current nine-turn source follows Lena on Tuesday: she asks the female server before sitting whether two hours of work is welcome; the server warns about lunch crowds; Lena offers to vacate the table, receives a paper slip with Wi-Fi password and a corner table with outlet, orders café con leche and pan dulce, asks after one hour when to order again, hears the server returns every half hour, and leaves a good tip with the bill. The archived generic laptop dialogue omits Lena, Tuesday, counter, slip, corner, both named foods, and the bill/tip ending. Japanese food, politeness, café and dictionary senses need qualified review.

savedPositionPolicy: Archived draft rows have no explicit stable row IDs and were not registered. Revision-scoped candidate IDs do not authorize saved-item or audio placement migration. Reordering requires a new revision.
reviewQuestionsInternal: Source English latte corresponds to Spanish café con leche; カフェラテ follows the English headword, while カフェオレ may better reflect the Spanish drink. Qualified food/source decision needed.
Pan dulce / sweet pastry is provisionally 甘いパン; qualified Mexican-food and Japanese teaching review should decide whether to retain パン・ドゥルセ or a contextual note.
Good tip / buena propina is rendered 多めのチップ, interpreting good as generous in amount; Japanese café tipping is locale-specific and requires qualified review.
The Spanish mesera marks a female server; 女性の店員さん states it once, then 店員さん continues naturally. English server does not mark gender.
Papelito and slip of paper support 小さな紙; 指し示します preserves points to the table without implying that the server escorts Lena.
満席になったら、テーブルを空けます preserves giving up the table if it fills, instead of offering it to a named person.
Next-order timing is rendered 次はいつ頃注文したらよろしいでしょうか; pragmatic register and politeness need qualified Japanese review.
お会計 is natural café bill phrasing, while 伝票 would name a bill slip; the source simply says bill.
Lena is transliterated レナ; name rendering is provisional.
